stories.headline: Three Departments Now Claim the Briefcase; None Will Describe It; Two Have Not Seen It
stories.byline: By our Ministry of Magic correspondent
body: The glowing briefcase recovered Tuesday from a bench in the Floo departure hall has attracted the formal attentions of three separate Ministry departments, sources confirmed this morning — an escalation that officials are describing as 'procedurally routine' and that procedurally routine officials are describing as 'not that at all.'

The Department of Mysteries filed the first claim at half seven; the Office of Unclassified Artefact Management filed a counter-claim at half seven and two minutes, citing prior jurisdiction over items that glow 'in a non-specific but persistent fashion.' A third claim arrived by internal post at nine from a department whose name the Ministry press office has asked us not to print, noting only that it does not officially exist and therefore cannot officially own anything, which they acknowledge is a complicated position.

The briefcase, for its part, has not moved. The hum, witnesses report, has deepened by approximately a minor third since Wednesday. A memo circulated suggesting someone open it. The memo has not been attributed.

stories.headline: Friday Account Review Proceeds Smoothly; Christine Suspects It Is Planning Something
body: A full morning of account reviews concluded at Gringotts today without a single escalation, disputed ledger entry, or goblin departing the table in the wrong direction. Senior Client Liaison Christine brought three prepared packets and a contingency fourth. None were required.

The goblins were, by all observable measures, pleasant. Christine has logged this in the incident register under 'anomalous' and recommended a precautionary review of Monday's bookings. 'Smooth Fridays,' she noted at close of business, 'are where the complicated Mondays come from.' The goblins, contacted for comment, said nothing and closed the window. This is considered, in Gringotts terms, a warm response.

stories.headline: Gorge Fog Advances Overnight; the Jeep's Eleven Ducks Observed Wearing Small Expressions of Seasonal Gravitas
body: Fog moved into the lower gorge hollows before dawn this morning, per the Eastern Ridgeline's seasonal notification filed yesterday — a development the Ridgeline describes as 'the rearrangement,' and which Steve describes as 'a sign.' The enchanted Jeep remains in the yard, eleven hatted ducks in position, and has not indicated whether it considers the season's turn an invitation or a warning.
Steve stood at the window for some time this morning. The hat log was not consulted. No expedition has been announced. The fog, sources close to the hollows confirm, is not in a hurry either.

stories.headline: Lucy Identified as Most Likely Author of the Unattributed Memo; Lucy Declines to Confirm; Lucy Has Already Left the Room
body: Following this morning's Ministry report that an unattributed memo circulated internally suggesting someone open the briefcase, investigative attention has turned — without any firm basis, but with considerable instinct — toward Lucy, who was in the vicinity of no Ministry office at any point and has an alibi described only as 'ironclad and, frankly, suspicious.'

Lucy has not commented. The memo, handwriting analysts note, bears no similarity to any known Ministry script, smells faintly of biscuit, and is considerably more direct than anything the Ministry has produced this decade. Inquiries continue.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Was observed near the owl post this morning and has produced documentation confirming she was not. The documentation is extremely thorough. This is itself suspicious.
Ellie: Spent a cheerful quarter-hour introducing herself to the fog through the kitchen window. The fog did not reciprocate. Ellie has scheduled a follow-up.
Jersey: Located the warmest available lap by six forty-five, logged it, and has not moved. Considers the briefcase situation someone else's problem, which is the correct assessment.
founding_editor_note: Glowing briefcase, three departments, nobody opens it — that's a load-bearing wall nobody wants to touch. I've seen this. You tap it and everything shifts. Leave it and order more plaster. — D.

in_brief.sport: Gringotts Invitational Ledger Sprint postponed pending clarification of which department currently owns the finish line.
in_brief.forecast: Fog through the gorge until further notice; eleven ducks steady; the briefcase hum expected to resolve into something that sounds like a question.

storyline_updates.title: The Briefcase
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: Three Ministry departments have filed competing claims of ownership — the Department of Mysteries, the Office of Unclassified Artefact Management, and an unnamed department that officially does not exist. An unattributed memo suggesting someone open the briefcase has circulated; its author is unknown (Lucy is the leading theory). The briefcase has not moved. The hum has deepened by a minor third. Day 3 should escalate toward an opening attempt — perhaps an Unspeakable is dispatched, or a junior clerk acts on the memo and reports something before the report is confiscated, or the briefcase briefly opens of its own accord and closes before anyone can confirm what they saw.
